subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures the city's flows in real time — energy, water, traffic, air, waste.

subsystems.name: Connectivity and edge compute
subsystems.role: moves and pre-processes data where it is generated, so the city is not one enormous central computer.
parts: edge servers in substations and cabinets

subsystems.name: City model / digital twin
subsystems.role: a shared, living representation of buildings, networks and people that every service can query.
parts: network graphs for roads, pipes, cables
simulation engines for traffic, hydraulics, power flow

subsystems.name: Learning layer
subsystems.role: forecasts demand, congestion and faults, and proposes settings.

subsystems.name: Control and actuation interfaces
subsystems.role: turns forecasts into real changes in the physical city.
parts: SCADA links to substations, pumps and traffic signals

subsystems.name: Governance and privacy layer
subsystems.role: decides who may see and change what, and keeps records.
parts: data-sharing agreements between agencies and utilities

buildSteps.title: Instrument one district
buildSteps.detail: Fit meters, flow sensors and cameras with published privacy rules, so there is real data with known gaps and failure modes.

buildSteps.title: Build the shared data layer
buildSteps.detail: Agree common schemas and time stamps, then stand up a time-series store and the first version of the 3D twin geometry.

buildSteps.title: Connect the control systems
buildSteps.detail: Give traffic signals, pumps and transformers a common read/write interface, with hardware interlocks that cannot be overridden by software.

buildSteps.title: Train local models
buildSteps.detail: Let each utility or district learn from its own data; only model updates, not raw records, leave the operator.

buildSteps.title: Federate and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Aggregate the models and run coupled what-if simulations in the twin — a street closure, a heatwave, a feeder fault.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop slowly
buildSteps.detail: Begin with advice to human operators, move to human-approved actions, and only then to automatic control of narrow, low-risk functions.

buildSteps.title: Harden for failure and attack
buildSteps.detail: Every loop needs a local fallback when the network drops, and red-teaming against poisoned data and spoofed sensors.

buildSteps.title: Extend across domains
buildSteps.detail: Add water, waste and buildings using interoperability standards, rather than rebuilding for each service.

prerequisites.why: planning-grade 3D models exist, but few are wired to live control systems and updated continuously.
proven on consumer devices such as phone keyboards; untested on utility control loops with hard safety requirements.
cheap sensors and low-power wide-area networks make dense instrumentation affordable.
traffic, hydraulic and power-flow simulators exist separately; running them together at city scale in real time is still research.
city indicator and data standards exist, but adoption is uneven and legal authority over shared data is fragmented.

pathway.milestone: district-scale digital twins used for planning, plus isolated smart metering and adaptive traffic signals
pathway.unlocks: data, models and trust built one service at a time.

pathway.milestone: city twins fed by live feeds, running in advisory mode for operators
pathway.unlocks: evidence that predictions are good enough to act on.

pathway.milestone: federated learning across several utilities under one governance framework
pathway.unlocks: cross-sector optimisation without pooling citizens' raw data.

pathway.milestone: coordinated control of energy, water and transport in a few cities
pathway.unlocks: measurable efficiency gains — with human authority retained over safety-critical decisions.
